extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, grantees, institutional staff)
extracted.subtask_description: A news-style summary of recent NIH policy, process, and resource updates relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards. Meant to inform investigators and institutional staff about changes that affect application content, review, and award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (including New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer models that are scientifically sound and that enhance human relevance and translational potential, but prioritize the model that best answers the specific research question. The entry references New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) as an area of focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format has been issued based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applications, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH (the page notifies the existence of the new format and that it should be used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout research
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations into applications, study design, and institutional practices. NIH has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts across the research enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who receive this designation were placed in the middle third of the study section under the modified process; this explains a review outcome category and its context (changes implemented last November after the lapse in appropriations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application structure
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH released a 6-minute overview video of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants planning PF5 submissions should review the overview to understand application format, key features, and the possibility of applications being split into linked awards post-review but prior to Just-in-Time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized NIH peer review (CSR consolidation) and its implications
rubrics_metrics.description: In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). The consolidation is reported to be strengthening efficiency, competition, and transparency in the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers should be aware that peer review operations and related processes may change due to centralization (e.g., review assignment, timelines, study section composition) and account for potential impacts on submission and review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor NIH program and funding changes (e.g., NIH Seed Fund / Small Business Program)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH announced that its Small Business Program (Seed Fund) is back in action, which is relevant news for innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business innovators and institutional tech-transfer/support offices should take note of program reinstatements and related application opportunities and timelines; monitor NIH news for when/how to apply.
